Jordan / Marissa,

Saw the attachments from Clearline. Finance will not clear the invoice until one of the following is provided (pick one):

1) Resale certificate with exact legal name that matches the W-9 and the EIN (signed and notarized OR DocuSigned with domain-verified email).
2) Corporate resolution or notarized letter on company letterhead explicitly stating that the name variants (e.g., "Clearline Logistics LLC" and "ClearLine Logistics, Inc.") represent the same legal entity tied to EIN XX-XXXXXXX. The resolution must be signed by an officer and notarized.
3) If the above cannot be provided quickly, a combination of: executed resale cert (even if name differs) + a government registry lookup (state business filing showing both names as DBAs or same EIN) + an authorized signatory affidavit.

Acceptance checklist:
- EIN match confirmed (we will verify via IRS crosswalk or state portal)
- Signer title and email domain on DocuSign match company domain OR notarization stamp visible
- Attachments legible, PDF preferred, file size < 10MB

If client commits to a DocuSign envelope with the CFO's company email (lynn.carter@clearline.com) and the envelope ID comes back to us (DocuSign link), we'll accept that as an electronic signature. Otherwise we must have a notarized/wet-ink document.

Please send this requirements list to the client and request ETA — I'll step in if they push for an exception.

Grace O'Connor

A notarized letter or a stamped corporate resolution will be airtight.

I can prepare a short notarized affidavit (on our letterhead) that references both registered names and the EIN; Clearline's legal can sign/notarize it. If you want the fastest path, re-executing the resale certificate in DocuSign with Lynn's CFO email is simplest — that removes ambiguity during verification.
